verdict.rationale: Factory documents Bring Your Own Machine, which lets you register your own VPS, workstation, or on-prem Linux/macOS/Windows server as a persistent Droid Computer. The Droid CLI and headless droid exec also run locally and in CI pipelines. Container deployment is not documented, and the evidence never says the agent control plane itself can be self-hosted rather than only attaching your machines to Factory's service. Missing for 10: documented container/Docker deployment, self-hosting of the orchestration/control plane, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can self-host agent infrastructure locally, in containers, or on my own VMs

citations.quote: Bring Your Own Machine (BYOM): You register a machine you already manage, such as a VPS, workstation, or on-prem server
Bring Your Own Machine (BYOM) lets you register your own Linux, macOS, or Windows machine as a Droid Computer.
Droid Computers **retain state**: installed packages, files, running services, and configuration all persist between sessions.
`droid exec` runs as a one-shot command that completes a task and exits, making it ideal for CI/CD pipelines, shell scripts, and batch processing.
